790601801.text: How about... We tear it down brick by brick and rebuild a new tower from scratch?

790601802.text: Hmm, no, no... That could send <color=#00E1FFFF>the lamp atop the tower</color> rolling right down...

790602403.text: Well, he is the first place venturers come to upon returning to the village.

790602404.text: Yes, he has collapsed, but I must do all I can to sort things out here. I cannot allow him to receive our returnees all by his lonesome.

790602405.text: And then there's Rozel. He has been drifting so far from home for so long — I absolutely must give him a hug the moment he returns!

790602406.text: So please, help me, dear guests — I will be here waiting for him, and for you too!

790602408.text: Venturers are explorers and wayfarers. They are those who are willing to leave everything behind and travel far abroad.

790602409.text: The distant places they wish to venture to include the far edge of starfalls, the other side of the rainbow.

790602410.text: And when they wish to return, this lighthouse is their only guide.

790602411.text: Traveling abroad is a good thing, of this there is no doubt. Yet there are some venturers who return from their travels changed.

790602412.text: Some mumble constantly about "value," and when they see a beautiful hat, they immediately ask how much it costs and what materials it's made from...

790602413.text: It's almost as if they cannot see the flower in that hat or the beautiful patterns woven into it.

790602414.text: Rozel says that it is because the many things venturers have seen color them, like ponds into which paint has been thrown.

790602415.text: I asked if it was a good or a bad thing, but he merely called it change — and that change is neither good nor bad.

790602416.text: I must confess that I simply do not understand...

790602418.text: Rozel was my neighbor. We'd chat, have tea, and play games together every day.

790602419.text: But one day, he told me that he wished to become a venturer, and soon, he began his travels.

790602420.text: First, he traveled the entire world, going to Constellation Metropole, Rainsong Pond, and the Forest of Blessings.

790602421.text: After that, he wanted to go still further abroad. So he built himself a little boat, planning to set sail for the far edge, where the stars fall.

790602422.text: He asked me to journey with him, but... I did not board. All I did was make him a windmill.

790602423.text: That way, he would at least sail faster while out at sea, and thus when it came time to return, his would be all the more swift.

790602424.text: Right! Rozel is unlike other venturers. He knows how to wear a hat and the reason why houses exist.

790602426.text: See you, honored guests! I shall be here waiting for Rozel, and for you.

790600101.text: Lighthouse... Lighthouse... I've got to haul you up, so my friends can find the way home... Phew... Just got to rest a bit before I do...

790600104.text: Hmm? What ho, you don't look like one of our neighbors from Brickstacks. A rarity indeed!

790600105.text: Esnoir's the name, and guarding this here Farseer Lighthouse's the game. It and I bid you welcome.

790600106.text: In truth, however, you've come at a most terrible time. T'was but a few scant moments ago when a monstrous dragon just ran by in a right hurry.

790600107.text: Clumsy and stumbling it was, and the two of us were in its wrathful path.

790600108.text: With a crack and a snap, both I and my poor lighthouse were bowled right over... And as you can see, I've regained my footing, but not so the lighthouse.

790600109.text: Huh... You sure are making light of that lighthouse being knocked down by that giant dragon, aren't you?

790600110.text: Aye, and I've tried all manner of ways to get him on his feet. Even the neighbors came to lend a hand.

790600111.text: But he simply refused to stand back up again. You'd almost think he had a temper, to throw such a tantrum...

790600112.text: Our neighbors still have to keep an eye on that dragon, so I'm on my own for the time being.

790600113.text: Agh! This is a terrible situation. With our lighthouse down for the count, we'll have no light... That means no return to the village for our venturers!

790602801.text: (Here, make the <color=#00E1FFFF>wish</color> you hold so dear, and the reasons for your prayer you must make clear.)

790601101.text: As Paimon cheers you on, you firmly support the lighthouse with your shoulder, plant your feet firmly, and...\nHeave ho!\n

790601102.text: The toppled tower salutes you stoically (and statically) with its weighty body — if nothing else, you courageously confronted this challenge.\nHeave ho, hup!\n

790601103.text: The lighthouse lies resolutely on the ground, silently extending its beneficence to you.\n

790601104.text: Heave ho— Ack!\nA dull crack sounds from near your hip, and you fall to the floor. It is only after lengthy and gentle ministrations on Paimon's part that you are again able to rise...\n

790601105.text: Best you think of some other way to do this...

790601201.text: After giving much thought as to where your strength would be best applied, you select a brick that seems like a firm handhold.\nGrabbing onto it, and to the sound of Paimon's cheers, you let loose a burst of tremendous effort to right the toppled tower...\n

790601202.text: ...Only to nearly be sent, friendly handhold-brick and all, tumbling off the island. Fortunately, Paimon manages to grab onto your clothes.\n

790601203.text: You... should probably consider an alternative...

790601301.text:
As Paimon cheers you on, you settle into a steady stance and tighten up your core, both hands grabbing onto the section of the toppled lighthouse best suited for gripping.
Adjust the distance... Breathe in... Stick out your chest... Put your strength into your shoulders... Wait, should it be your shoulders or your back?
Well, whatever the case, time to put your back and/or shoulders into it! Heave ho!

790601302.text: ...As Paimon comforts you and the lighthouse looks on, you let go for now.\n

790601303.text: Just... think of something else already, would you...

subQuests.subQuestName: Find a way to make the lighthouse... stand up?

790600301.text: Whoa! The lamp really came off! I—It isn't broken now, is it?

790600303.text: Eh? Huh. You're right. But why is it still shining even after being removed?

790600307.text: Never mind that for now. Let's put the lamp back before anyone sees us!

790600309.text: Uh oh, uh oh, this has gotta be the lightkeeper!

790600305.text: What? Hey! Don't just give it to Paimon! Someone's definitely watching this thing — they're gonna rake us over the coals for sure!

790600306.text: Oh, what do we do now... Huh? Wait a minute. Why is this lamp still shining, even after being removed?

790600201.text: Whoa! The lamp really came off! I—It isn't broken now, is it?

790600203.text: Eh? Huh. You're right. But why is it still shining even after being removed?

790600207.text: So the reason the lighthouse shone so brightly is that there was a super bright "light" hanging in the lighthouse...

790600208.text: That said, aren't light sources usually super complex mechanisms?

790600209.text: Eh, that's not important! Since this one can be removed normally, that works for us!

790600210.text: Esnoir mentioned earlier that he needs to get the lighthouse standing back up again because he wants to put the light someplace high so more people can see it...

790600211.text: In that case, let's just hang it up somewhere high, right now!

790600212.text: Hehe, that's what Paimon was thinking too! ...Y'know, wouldn't everyone be able to see it if we could hang it up in the sky?

790600205.text: What? Wait! Foisting it on Paimon won't stop us both from getting scolded!

790600206.text: Oh, what do we do now... Huh? Wait a minute. Why is this lamp still shining, even after being removed?

790600501.text: This tree proves surprisingly amenable to ornaments of the lamp variety, and you have it hung up in no time.

790600502.text: That should do it! The light should shine far and wide now.

790600505.text: We wait, of course! Maybe those venturers have seen the light already, and are on the way back as we speak.

790600506.text: Huh... Nothing's happened. Not a person has returned.

790600507.text: Hello, you two. Not to disturb you or anything, but what were you intending to do by hanging that light up again?

790600510.text: I see. I've heard about the issue with Esnoir and the lighthouse as well, and this idea is a good one. However...

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the highest island and hang the lamp at its highest point

790600601.text: Hmm, three statues, and it looks like we're gonna have to offer them two more gifts.

790600602.text: But what should we offer? Paimon hasn't a clue.

790600604.text: If it should be related to the wish, we should offer that lamp.

790600605.text: That makes sense! Esnoir's wish is to see this lamp hung high for all to see, right?

790600606.text: Well, that just about clears "armor," but we don't have any clue where to begin with "weapons."

790600607.text: It could be a sword, a polearm... There's way too many options.

790600609.text: Eh? No, no, hold on! Panuelle placed a dragon's scale here before! So this "weapon" should have something to do with dragons too, right?

790600610.text: No worries, I have dragon-related weapons too, don't I?

790600611.text: Paimon means something related to dragons in *this world.* This. World!

790600615.text: And that might be true enough, but...

790600613.text: That makes sense. Panuelle's dragon scale must have been the "armor."

790600614.text: That means the "weapon" must also have something to do with dragons.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the highest island and hang the lamp at its highest point

790600401.text: Chauvigne... Why are you still angry? *sigh* Perhaps you really shouldn't have ventured outside...

790600402.text: Err, hello there. Did you plant this tree? We'd like to, uh...

790600404.text: That is to say, "hang a lamp on it."

790600406.text: A lamp? Well, putting one up would be nice. Some warm light might do Chauvigne's mood some good. Might even put us on speaking terms again!

790600407.text: Please do lend us a hand then — and if I may lend you one in turn, just say the word and it shall be so.

790600408.text: #Nice! Smooth sailing so far, eh, {NICKNAME}? C'mon, let's get this lamp hung up.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the highest island and hang the lamp at its highest point

790600801.text: (Here, make the <color=#00E1FFFF>wish</color> you hold so dear, and the reasons for your prayer you must make clear.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the "Whispering Isle" and make a wish to the three "goddess" statues

790601001.text: Hmm, three statues, and it looks like we're gonna have to offer them two more gifts.

790601002.text: But what should we offer? Paimon hasn't a clue.

790601004.text: If it should be related to the wish, we should offer that lamp.

790601005.text: That makes sense! Esnoir's wish is to see this lamp hung high for all to see, right?

790601006.text: Well, that just about clears "armor," but we don't have any clue where to begin with "weapons."

790601007.text: It could be a sword, a polearm... There's way too many options.

790601010.text: Dragon-related stuff... Hang on. Didn't we pick up something that resembles a horn from inside that mountain?

790601011.text: That's right, and it looked like...

790601012.text: Like a sword! That's gotta be the "weapon" we're looking for!

790601013.text: Th—That sounds sensible, and looks sensible too!

790601014.text: The point is, the whole idea is most sensible!

790601015.text: On point! The problem is, though, that Panuelle's wish wasn't granted even after making a wish using the dragon scale...

790601016.text: But the scale and horn are our only clues right now, so we may as well give it a try.

790601017.text: That said, Whispering Isle is pretty big, huh? The three goddess statues up there are huge, too.

790601018.text: If this was an ordinary adventure story, there would be mysterious treasures hidden under the statues or something.

790601019.text: Hehe... On that note, think we should take a closer look around? You never know when we'll find something nice.

790601501.text: (Present you now your <color=#00E1FFFF>armor</color> strong, that guards your heart lest it go wrong.)

790601502.text: This should be the dragon scale that Panuelle used to wish, then?

790601504.text: Really? Huh... If nothing else, at least we know he did come here to wish before.

790601506.text: Hrrgh... Nope, it's no use. The scale won't come off. Guess the goddess liked the gift after all.

790601401.text: (Offer here your <color=#00E1FFFF>weapon</color> bright, dispel the dense daze as light does night.)

790602901.text: (Offer here your <color=#00E1FFFF>weapon</color> bright, dispel the dense daze as light does night.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the "toytanium mines" and search for the "weapon"

790602501.text: Hey, the sword's come out... G—Guess we've got these gophers to thank, huh?

790602502.text: This sure is a mysterious place... But either way, we've got the sword, so all's well.

790602505.text: A horn? You mean like one from that dragon?

790602506.text: Hmm. If scales are a dragon's "armor," then we could consider horns its "weapons"...

790602507.text: Not that we've found any other clues, anyway. Let's go back and offer it to that goddess. And then we've just gotta hope that she likes our gifts...

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the "Whispering Isle" and make a wish to the three "goddess" statues

790603001.text: (Present you now your <color=#00E1FFFF>armor</color> strong, that guards your heart lest it go wrong.)

790601601.text: Lighthouse... Lighthouse... I've got to haul you up, so my friends can find the way home... Phew... Just got to rest a bit before I do...

790601604.text: Hmm? What ho, you don't look like one of our neighbors from Brickstacks. A rarity indeed!

790601605.text: Esnoir's the name, and guarding this here Farseer Lighthouse's the game. It and I bid you welcome.

790601606.text: In truth, however, you've come at a most terrible time. T'was but a few scant moments ago when a monstrous dragon just ran by in a right hurry.

790601607.text: Clumsy and stumbling it was, and the two of us were in its wrathful path.

790601608.text: With a crack and a snap, both I and my poor lighthouse were bowled right over... And as you can see, I've regained my footing, but not so the lighthouse.

790601609.text: Oh boy. So Mini Durin knocked this lighthouse over just by passing through...

790601610.text: Aye, and I've tried all manner of ways to get him on his feet. Even the neighbors came to lend a hand.

790601611.text: But he simply refused to stand back up again. You'd almost think he had a temper, to throw such a tantrum...

790601612.text: Our neighbors still have to keep an eye on that dragon, so I'm on my own for the time being.

790601613.text: Agh! This is a terrible situation. With our lighthouse down for the count, we'll have no light... That means no return to the village for our venturers!

790600701.text: Esnoir! Oh, it's good to see you! I knew I could trust you... and the light that you shone my way!

790600702.text: I gave you my word, dear friend — and now, you're back. As for the light, however, you have our two guests to thank.

790600703.text: Skies above, that was you, then? I thought you had been stranded on that island when I saw you on my return trip, which is why I invited you onboard...

790600704.text: Words fail to describe how thankful I am to you. Had that radiance not reached my ship, I'm sure I would have been utterly lost at sea.

790600705.text: Also... What happened to your lighthouse, Esnoir? What happened to this place? What exactly did I miss?

790600706.text: Esnoir gesticulates wildly as he explains the events that transpired to Rozel...

790600707.text: A dragon crashed into the village — and another into the waterfall behind it?

790600708.text: That... really is a lot. I'm going to have to ask you to give me all the details when you've got the time.

790600709.text: Well, I have the time right now — I have time any time, in fact! I've managed to clean up a little area where we can have some tea and cakes... and enjoy the fragrance of the flowers while we're at it.

790600710.text: Really? Then that would be no problem at all. In fact, I've been looking forward to this. I'll show you the new samples I've collected, too.

790600711.text: You will not believe all the different types of flowers and bugs I've encountered. It's just a shame that my bag is so small — I shall bring a larger one next time for sure!

790600712.text: Next time... You'll leave again, I presume?

790600713.text: ...Do not worry. Our time together is lengthy still, Esnoir. The time we have now is more than sufficient for me to tell you about all the new things I've seen, I assure you.

790600715.text: Yes. I am a venturer. To venture is my calling.

790600716.text: Don't go, Rozel! Have you not noticed how some of your colleagues become... strange when they return?

790600717.text: They fret about the "value" of carpets and hats... but not at all about which is more beautiful or intricately made...

790600718.text: ...Don't be angry, Esnoir. We can speak about this later.

790600719.text: I brought you flower seeds from outside — ones with contours and colors I'm sure you've never seen before.

790600720.text: Ah, yes. Dear guests, you too should take some of these marvelous new gifts I've obtained from outside. Consider them a token of my gratitude.

790600721.text: Thank you for lighting the way for my ship, and also for taking care of Esnoir.

790600722.text: Now that the light illuminates the way, I'm sure the other venturers will also begin returning to the village.

790600723.text: I hope they can rest well. After all, there are many "far off places" that await their exploration still.

790600901.text: You mean to climb this tree? Well, be careful, then.

790600902.text: Stepping on those smashed stone fragments after falling out of it would be quite unpleasant.

790602001.text: (Here, make the <color=#00E1FFFF>wish</color> you hold so dear, and the reasons for your prayer you must make clear.)

790602101.text: (Offer here your <color=#00E1FFFF>weapon</color> bright, dispel the dense daze as light does night.)

790602201.text: (Present you now your <color=#00E1FFFF>armor</color> strong, that guards your heart lest it go wrong.)

790602601.text: Hmm, three statues, and it looks like we're gonna have to offer them two more gifts.

790602602.text: But what should we offer? Paimon hasn't a clue.

790602604.text: If it should be related to the wish, we should offer that lamp.

790602605.text: That makes sense! Esnoir's wish is to see this lamp hung high for all to see, right?

790602606.text: Well, that just about clears "armor," but we don't have any clue where to begin with "weapons."

790602607.text: It could be a sword, a polearm... There's way too many options.

790602609.text: Eh? No, no, hold on! Panuelle placed a dragon's scale here before! So this "weapon" should have something to do with dragons too, right?

790602610.text: No worries, I have dragon-related weapons too, don't I?

790602611.text: Paimon means something related to dragons in *this world.* This. World!

790602615.text: And that might be true enough, but...

790602619.text: Let's head over to the mountain the dragon destroyed first, shall we?

790602620.text: Yeah, we're not doing anything sitting around here and thinking. Panuelle said that the dragon crashed into that mountain and smashed it, right?

790602621.text: If we're lucky, we might find some draconic bits and bobs — teeth, horns, or maybe other stuff like that...

790602622.text: Ho, now those sure sound like weapons!

790602623.text: Right? Let's go, then! And let's hope that mountain isn't as "broken" as he said...

790602624.text: That said, Whispering Isle is pretty big, huh? The three goddess statues up there are huge, too.

790602625.text: If this was an ordinary adventure story, there would be mysterious treasures hidden under the statues or something.

790602626.text: Hehe... On that note, think we should take a closer look around? You never know when we'll find something nice.

790602613.text: That makes sense. Panuelle's dragon scale must have been the "armor."

790602614.text: That means the "weapon" must also have something to do with dragons.

790602616.text: Why don't we go talk this one out with Mini Durin?

790602617.text: Huh? Eh, Paimon thinks we'd better not. What are we gonna say, anyway? "Oh, could you spare us some scales, or a horn, pretty please?"

790602618.text: That just... doesn't seem very polite...

790602701.text: This tree proves surprisingly amenable to ornaments of the lamp variety, and you have it hung up in no time.

790602702.text: That should do it! The light should shine far and wide now.

790602705.text: We wait, of course! Maybe those venturers have seen the light already, and are on the way back as we speak.

790602706.text: Huh... Nothing's happened. Not a person has returned.

790602707.text: Hello, you two. Not to disturb you or anything, but what were you intending to do by hanging that light up again?

790602710.text: I see. I've heard about the issue with Esnoir and the lighthouse as well, and this idea is a good one. However...
